findings.reason: a node implementing the section literally adds a flat key, which releases `claude-sub`'s three reserves as well and makes the orchestrator lanes the section explicitly exempts unheld, so the deliverable's central distinction ("a group that declares nothing keeps today's holds and reserves") is unimplementable without the plan naming a per-group declaration shape.
findings.text: §48's deliverable reads "A budget group whose flight declares `pace: advisory`" and its landing step (snapshot line 625) is "the host flight declares `codex-sub` advisory and leaves `claude-sub` as it is", but a flight declares one flat `BudgetConfig` block (`FlightConfig.budget: BudgetConfig | None`, `reckon/_flight_schema.py:219`, whose fields at `reckon/_flight_schema.py:623-637`: `utilisation_ceiling_pct`, `resume_reserve_pct`, `coordinator_reserve_pct`, `bookend_reserve_pct`, `pace_multiple` are all flat fields with no per-group structure), group membership is derived only from each backend's `budget_group` slot (`reckon/crew/budget_group.py:89-105`, and `effective_block(config, group, ...)` returns `config["budget"]` unchanged for every group unless a lift is in force (`reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:613-615`; `budget_group.py:210-218`). So a flight-scoped `pace:` key applies to every group of that flight, including the orchestrator lanes the section says are to be left alone, and the done-when's fourth case — "A group that declares nothing, at the same figures, is held by pace and by its 92% ceiling" — cannot be stood up in one flight beside an advisory group; the schema write paths are cited but the declaration's shape is never stated

findings.reason: the section's write paths already name `reckon/pace_report.py` "where `pace_hold` now lives", so a node that reaches the failing case finds the second edit point inside its own grant; naming the caller would sharpen the mechanism sentence but sends no node anywhere it is not already authorised to write.
findings.text: the sentence "The advisory rule is composed in `effective_block` beside the lift and review-exclusion rules, so dispatch, resume prediction and the picker read it through the one resolution they already share" names the resolution but not the reader that decides the pace hold, which is `pace_hold(entry, role)` reading the group entry's allowance (`reckon/crew/budget_report` path: `reckon/pace_report.py:1252-1293`, allowance built by `reckon/crew/pace.py:167-201` from the effective block's `pace_multiple` alone, with no advisory field), so composing the rule in `effective_block` alone leaves case 1 ("an advisory group at 96% with a burn multiple of 19 is not held for an implement dispatch") failing until the advisory sign is carried into that allowance
